en.title: Mutual Friend Recommendation
en.description:
Users are numbered 0..n−1, and the input gives undirected friendships. For each user y, among users who are neither y nor a friend of y, choose the one with the most mutual friends; break ties by the smallest number. If there is no candidate, the result is -1.

The original problem's ordering rule and the limit of at most 15 friends per person are explicit; this site adds no duplicate edges and the input/output protocol.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/weride#4-friend-recommendation-system-max-common-friends (fixed statement fingerprint 714fa067c86636fe872c62ad6ef9e5113a22f11336c9cc098921db1095093cc3). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site are as described in the statement and are not claimed to be rules of the original site.
en.input: The first line contains n m (1≤n≤100000); each of the next m lines is a pair of distinct user numbers. Friendships have no duplicates, are undirected, and each person has at most 15 friends.
en.output: Output n recommended numbers in order of user number.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof, and complexity.
hints: You only need to accumulate occurrence counts of two-hop neighbors. If there is no two-hop candidate, every non-friend candidate has 0 mutual friends, so take the smallest available number.
